comparisons.peer_summary: Data Center net revenue increased 94% to $12.6 billion in 2024 from $6.5 billion in 2023, primarily driven by higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs. Operating income rose to $3.5 billion in 2024 from $1.3 billion in 2023, mainly due to higher revenue partially offset by increased R&D investment.
comparisons.comparison: The target (Intel) reports a decrease in Client and Data Group (CNP) revenue driven by lower intersegment ASPs and back-end services, partially offset by higher wafer volume. In contrast, AMD’s Data Center segment reports a significant revenue increase driven by higher sales of GPUs and CPUs. While both companies operate in the data center/server market, their 2024 performance diverged sharply: Intel faced ASP headwinds and volume declines in its intersegment business, whereas AMD benefited from strong demand for its Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs, leading to substantial growth.

comparisons.peer_topic: Semiconductor Solutions segment operating income drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Operating income from the semiconductor solutions segment increased, primarily driven by revenue growth from networking products (including AI networking products), partially offset by lower net revenue from broadband and server storage products.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures analyze segment operating income drivers related to product demand shifts. Intel's CNP segment operating income is implicitly impacted by the described revenue decrease (lower ASPs and volume). Broadcom’s Semiconductor Solutions segment operating income increased, primarily driven by revenue growth from AI networking products, partially offset by lower revenue in broadband and server storage. Both companies highlight the influence of product mix (e.g., AI-related products vs. legacy/other products) on their financial performance, though Intel reports a revenue decline while Broadcom reports operating income growth.
